nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why do fashion rental platforms focus on offering designer brands?
nodes.answer: Fashion rental platforms focus on offering designer brands because designer brands are believed to be more durable and of higher quality. This quality allows the garments to withstand being worn by multiple users and being dry-cleaned more frequently than when owned by a single consumer.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Minimalist lifestyles|Capsule wardrobes_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is one uncertainty related to the volume of garments that rental platforms own?
nodes.answer: The uncertainty lies in overlooking the volume of garments that rental platforms own to run their businesses.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Minimalist lifestyles|Capsule wardrobes_qna_002
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the purpose of the Fashion ID tool in the fashion suturing process?
nodes.answer: The Fashion ID tool serves to help participants situate themselves by describing their favourite fashion artifact, reflecting on the meanings and values embedded in such objects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Minimalist lifestyles|Capsule wardrobes_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How were text-based clothing diaries utilized in conjunction with wardrobe interviews to gather data on garment use and laundry care practices?
nodes.answer: Text-based clothing diaries were used to gather specific data on garment use and laundry care practices, exposing participants' everyday care competencies and skills. These diary entries were also employed as a prompt during wardrobe interviews to elicit more in-depth narratives and fully uncover everyday practices.
